project.name: AgentNest
project.description: AgentNest is a Turkish-first, mobile-first Instagram operations assistant for small businesses. It maintains verified business knowledge, drafts grounded customer DM replies, prepares and schedules content with explicit approvals, and reports outcomes with credential-free simulated integrations.

nodes.name: health.py
nodes.summary: Tracks transient provider failure windows and circuit cooldowns, recovers healthy accounts, and handles reauthorization or capability loss with manager notifications.

nodes.name: record_success
nodes.summary: Any success resets the failure counter and its window. A success on a degraded account (the half-open probe after the cooldown) closes the circuit.

nodes.name: recover
nodes.summary: degraded -> connected: tell the managers and make the queued replies due.

nodes.name: extend_cooldown
nodes.summary: The account is still failing: leave it alone for another cooldown.

nodes.name: record_transient_failure
nodes.summary: Count one transient failure (plan H10); open the circuit at the threshold.

nodes.name: handle_auth_error
nodes.summary: The token is no longer valid: the account needs the owner to connect it again.

nodes.name: handle_permission_error
nodes.summary: A required permission is missing: capability (messaging, or the publishing capability of a content type) is unavailable until it is granted. Tells the connection managers.

nodes.name: health_check.py
nodes.summary: Probes degraded accounts outside long-lived transactions and records recovery or renewed cooldown, exposing account IDs for periodic scheduling.

nodes.name: run_health_check
nodes.summary: Reads the degraded account profile outside a database transaction, then records recovery, renewed cooldown or required reauthorization.

nodes.name: _conclude
nodes.summary: Recovers an account after a successful profile probe, marks revoked credentials for reauthorization or extends the degraded cooldown.

nodes.name: degraded_account_ids
nodes.summary: (workspace_id, account_id) of every degraded account (the scheduler's view).

nodes.name: jobs.py
nodes.summary: Registers send, publish, reconciliation, account recovery and health jobs. Sweeps abandoned in-progress operations into reconciliation and emits simulated send echoes.

nodes.name: send_reply
nodes.summary: Executes the typed send-reply job and translates its lifecycle outcome into worker retry or reschedule behavior.

nodes.name: _publish_dead
nodes.summary: The publish job is dead: the item must not stay scheduled for ever (G10).

nodes.name: publish_content
nodes.summary: Publish one version of a scheduled item (workflows.md section E step 6).

nodes.name: _reconcile_publish_dead
nodes.summary: Concludes exhausted publish reconciliation as unconfirmed without repeating the publication.

nodes.name: reconcile_publish
nodes.summary: Read the container of a publish whose outcome is unknown and conclude (never a blind retry). While the container is still processing, or an unknown outcome came up again, the same job row is looked at again later, until the operation's deadline ends it.

nodes.name: resume_account
nodes.summary: The account is connected again: make the queued replies that can still go out due now.

nodes.name: account_health_check
nodes.summary: Probe a degraded account (workflows.md G.2). The next probe is the next periodic tick, so a failed check is a result (the cooldown starts again), not a job failure.

nodes.name: enqueue_health_checks
nodes.summary: Enqueues health checks for operations.

nodes.name: reconcile_send
nodes.summary: Runs a bounded send-reconciliation check and reschedules unresolved evidence without issuing another send.

nodes.name: demo_emit_echo
nodes.summary: Simulator only: the echo webhook Instagram would send for a message we sent, delivered through the real ingestion path (signed, deduplicated, processed by the worker).

nodes.name: _sent_message
nodes.summary: The simulator's record of what this operation sent: by id, or (when the answer was lost) by recipient and text.

nodes.name: reconcile_stuck_operations
nodes.summary: An operation that stayed in_progress (the worker died mid-call) may or may not have had its effect: make it outcome_unknown and reconcile it, never repeat it blindly (INV-05). A reply goes to reconcile_send; a publish (G11) to reconcile_publish.

nodes.name: _unstick_send
nodes.summary: Turns an abandoned in-progress send into an unknown outcome and queues reconciliation rather than sending again.

nodes.name: _unstick_publish
nodes.summary: Moves a stuck publishing operation into reconciliation using its committed container checkpoint.

nodes.name: enqueue_stuck_check
nodes.summary: Enqueues stuck check for operations.

nodes.name: publish.py
nodes.summary: Executes scheduled publishing with committed ledger and container checkpoints around transaction-free provider calls. Reconciles ambiguous results through container state, with quota deferral, bounded polling, retries and holds.

nodes.name: _skip
nodes.summary: Returns a structured skipped-work outcome with its reason.

nodes.name: capability_for
nodes.summary: feed_image needs publish_feed_image; story_image, publish_story_image.

nodes.name: execute_publish
nodes.summary: Publish version of the item once. Safe to call again: the ledger, the item's status and the container decide what, if anything, still has to happen.

nodes.name: reconcile_publish
nodes.summary: One reconciliation check of an outcome_unknown publish: read the container back.

nodes.name: abandon_publish
nodes.summary: The publish_content job is dead (on_dead): make sure the item does not stay scheduled for ever. An attempt that may have reached the provider is left to reconciliation; everything else becomes failed. No commit.

nodes.name: abandon_reconcile
nodes.summary: The reconcile_publish job is dead: nothing could confirm the publish. Reported as OUTCOME_UNCONFIRMED and never repeated. No commit.

nodes.name: _item
nodes.summary: Loads a workspace content item, optionally locking its row before publishing decisions.

nodes.name: _operation_by_key
nodes.summary: Finds the ledger operation identified by the version-specific publishing idempotency key.

nodes.name: _operation_by_id
nodes.summary: Loads the workspace ledger operation by its identifier for reconciliation.

nodes.name: _read_quota
nodes.summary: The provider's publishing quota (plan.md G8), read before T1 and with no transaction open. None when nothing is due or the read failed: the provider enforces its limit at publish time anyway (a rate-limited answer is retried like any other).

nodes.name: _fetch_media
nodes.summary: The permalink of a published post, best effort (a read: no transaction is open).

nodes.name: _begin
nodes.summary: Locks the due content item, validates its version, approval, account, deadline and media, then prepares a uniquely keyed publishing operation before external calls.

nodes.name: _reschedule
nodes.summary: Nothing is tried now (no quota, an open circuit): the item waits for retry_at as retry_scheduled and the attempt counter is untouched.

nodes.name: _text
nodes.summary: Selects the provider caption value appropriate to the content type, omitting captions for stories.

nodes.name: _prepared
nodes.summary: Copies the locked publishing item, operation and account values into the immutable data needed after the transaction.

nodes.name: _create_operation
nodes.summary: The ledger row of this version (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then FOR UPDATE).

nodes.name: _quota_retry_at
nodes.summary: When the quota has room again (plan.md G8): the instant the oldest post that has to leave the window does, 24 h after it was published. PublishingQuota carries no timestamps, so the times come from the account's published items; if they do not cover the count, an hour from now.

nodes.name: _release_waiting_operation
nodes.summary: Cancels a pending operation or fails a retry-wait operation when the associated content can no longer execute.

nodes.name: _refuse
nodes.summary: The item cannot go out and never will (overdue, approval no longer valid, media gone): failed. The table has no scheduled -> failed or retry_scheduled -> publishing -> shortcut, so the item takes start first inside the same transaction.

nodes.name: _hold
nodes.summary: The account is not usable at the due time: on_hold (ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE). The owner re-approves, because the schedule may have passed (workflows.md section G.2).

nodes.name: _drive
nodes.summary: Everything after T1: container, polling, publish, outcome. No transaction is open during any provider call or sleep.

nodes.name: _create_container
nodes.summary: Creates a provider media container from the prepared image reference and caption, then stores its ID as a committed recovery checkpoint.

nodes.name: _poll
nodes.summary: Wait for the container (plan.md G9): every 10 s for up to 5 minutes, the elapsed time taken from the Clock, the sleeper injected, a heartbeat after each wait. Returns what the container became, or the outcome of an error or of the timeout.

nodes.name: _locked
nodes.summary: Item, operation, account (in that order) of a run after T1, locked.

nodes.name: _store_container
nodes.summary: [T2] Commit the container id (or forget it), so a re-run uses the stored one.

nodes.name: _finish
nodes.summary: Records the provider publish result in a fresh transaction and concludes success or delegates the provider error to lifecycle handling.

nodes.name: _record_published
nodes.summary: The post is out: the operation succeeded, the item is published (immutable from now on, INV-17), the approvers are told, the account's failure counter is reset.

nodes.name: mark_unknown
nodes.summary: The outcome is not known: never publish again to find out. The item stays publishing (the UI shows "checking" from the operation) and reconcile_publish reads the container.

nodes.name: _poll_timeout
nodes.summary: The container is still processing after the polling budget: hand over to reconciliation.

nodes.name: _fail_now
nodes.summary: Locks current publish state in a fresh transaction and records an immediate publishing failure.

nodes.name: _fail
nodes.summary: Marks the operation and associated work failed, records the reason and emits the relevant user notification.

nodes.name: _record_error
nodes.summary: Map a provider error to the ledger and the item (workflows.md section G.1).

nodes.name: _map_error
nodes.summary: Maps publishing errors to retry, permanent failure, account hold or unknown-outcome reconciliation while preserving side-effect safety.

nodes.name: _conclude
nodes.summary: Concludes the provider result under fresh row locks and updates the operation lifecycle without blindly repeating an ambiguous side effect.

nodes.name: PublishOutcome
nodes.summary: Carries Publish Outcome data for operations: kind, detail, error_code, retry_after_seconds, run_at.

nodes.name: _Prepared
nodes.summary: What the calls after T1 need, copied out of the locked rows.

nodes.name: _Quota
nodes.summary: Carries Quota data for operations: used, limit.

nodes.name: _Quota.exhausted
nodes.summary: Reports whether the provider quota usage has reached its limit.

nodes.name: _Env
nodes.summary: The injected collaborators of one execution.

nodes.name: _Env.provider_for
nodes.summary: Uses the injected Instagram provider or builds the configured adapter for the prepared account kind.

nodes.name: _Polled
nodes.summary: Carries Polled data for operations: state, media_id.

nodes.name: reconcile.py
nodes.summary: Matches send echoes and checks recent provider outbound messages to settle ambiguous sends without sending again. Gives up as unconfirmed after the bounded reconciliation window.

nodes.name: match_echo
nodes.summary: Is this echo the one of a send of ours? (Registered with inbox.echoes below.)

nodes.name: reconcile_send
nodes.summary: One reconciliation check. Returns resolved (nothing left to do), sent, unconfirmed or rescheduled.

nodes.name: _conclude
nodes.summary: Concludes the provider result under fresh row locks and updates the operation lifecycle without blindly repeating an ambiguous side effect.

nodes.name: resolution.py
nodes.summary: Centralizes delivered-reply bookkeeping and ledger transitions for known, unknown and late-confirmed sends, updating messages, drafts, attention, audit and notifications.

nodes.name: text_sha256
nodes.summary: Hashes outgoing UTF-8 reply text for matching send evidence without copying message text into ledger metadata.

nodes.name: set_operation
nodes.summary: Apply a state-machine event to the ledger row (the row is locked by the caller).

nodes.name: lock_conversation
nodes.summary: Locks conversation for operations.

nodes.name: record_delivered
nodes.summary: The reply is out: store it as a message, close the draft, update the conversation.

nodes.name: resolve_unknown_as_sent
nodes.summary: An echo or the lookup proved the message was delivered.

nodes.name: resolve_unconfirmed
nodes.summary: Nothing confirmed the send within the window. It is reported and never repeated: the message may well have been delivered, and a duplicate to a customer is worse than a miss.

nodes.name: record_late_delivery
nodes.summary: An echo of a send we had given up on: the message *was* delivered. It is recorded as the business's own message (not misread as a reply typed in the Instagram app), the draft keeps its terminal state, and the audit trail says what happened.

nodes.name: _one

nodes.name: r1_account
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by account connection and messaging capability without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r2_window
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by messaging-window deadline with the safety margin without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r3_takeover
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by human takeover without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r4_language
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by unsupported reply language without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r5_sensitive
nodes.summary: The union of the model's flags and the keyword flags: no model output removes a reason.

nodes.name: r6_keyword
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by configured escalation keywords without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r7_model
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by model inability to answer or request for a human without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r8_facts
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by unusable required facts or failed rendering without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r9_grounding
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by deterministic claim-grounding failure without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r10_llm
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by provider or budget failures without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r11_attachment
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by attachment-only messages without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r12_injection
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by possible prompt injection without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: _has_class
nodes.summary: Checks class in the policy workflow, coordinating intent_action_class.

nodes.name: _policy_findings
nodes.summary: A policy finding, plus CONTAINS_<CLASS> when the mode came from a quoted fact's class rather than the intent's own (the strictest-class rule, explained).

nodes.name: r13_automation_off
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by disabled effective automation without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r14_policy_approval
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by action-class approval requirements without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r15_readiness
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by incomplete automation readiness without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r16_rate_guard
nodes.summary: Adds the deterministic policy finding required by automatic reply-rate limits without relaxing other rule outcomes.

nodes.name: r17_unsupported_intent
nodes.summary: An intent with no action class that is not one of the always-human ones (other, or no intent at all because no model ran and nothing else already explains it).

tour.title: Understand the Product
tour.description: Start with the project overview: AgentNest helps small businesses manage Instagram knowledge, customer replies and scheduled content in a Turkish-first experience. The architecture document connects the workspace interface, FastAPI API and background worker, giving you a map for the workflows that follow. The current local demonstration uses simulated integrations.

tour.title: Trace the Runtime Entrypoints
tour.description: With the process map in mind, follow the API factory as it installs middleware, routes, startup checks and handler registration. The worker entrypoint initializes the same application foundations for background execution, while typed settings select configuration and reject unsafe production combinations. These two processes share domain services rather than duplicating business policy.

tour.title: Establish Workspace Boundaries
tour.description: Before following a business workflow, understand how explicit workspace and actor context travels through requests and jobs. Authentication services establish identity, and SQLAlchemy sessions and tenant-safe model conventions support isolated persistence. The injected UTC clock is a widely shared dependency that makes time-sensitive workflows reproducible, while the data-model document explains durable relationships and constraints.

tour.title: Explore the User Interfaces
tour.description: The React entrypoint mounts the providers and routes that expose the backend workflows to authenticated workspace members. The application shell makes navigation, notifications and commands available across desktop and phone layouts, while the simulation banner keeps the integration mode visible. The public landing application is built separately and presents a bilingual demonstration and pilot signup rather than participating in workspace operations.

tour.title: Ground Work in Verified Facts
tour.description: The workspace first needs durable business knowledge before replies or content can make trustworthy claims. Knowledge services manage versioned facts and candidate acceptance with permissions and audit history; the renderer substitutes only usable facts and records their inserted spans. Impact propagation links a changed fact to dependent drafts, posts and reusable answers, making later approval invalidation understandable.

tour.title: Bound the AI Proposals
tour.description: Building on verified facts, the AI runtime requests structured proposals under tracing, budgets and typed retry rules. Trusted templates are separated from labelled untrusted message data, and closed schemas constrain the shapes returned for commands, replies and content. Task-specific prompts and semantic checks produce drafts for deterministic services to validate; they do not give the model publishing or sending authority.

tour.title: Authorize Exact Proposed Changes
tour.description: Commands turn the bounded proposals into interpretations, clarification requests and explicit decisions. Approval services bind authorization to an exact payload and version, reject stale or consumed grants, and execute subject callbacks atomically as the human decider. This boundary explains why changing a draft or its dependencies requires renewed authorization before an external effect.

tour.title: Follow the Reply Workflow
tour.description: The inbox combines the knowledge, AI and approval boundaries into grounded reply drafts. Its workflow rejects stale drafting plans, applies deterministic safety rules and attaches an exact-payload grant or a pending authorization. Manual edits, takeover and release recheck messaging eligibility and text versions, while model signals can add restrictions without weakening those guards.

tour.title: Prepare and Schedule Content
tour.description: Content applies the same approval discipline to a longer lifecycle of generated drafts, edits and scheduling. Generation separates preparation and provider work from draft storage, while grounding checks captions and overlays against usable facts and records governing dependencies. Validation checks media, account capabilities, scheduling and quota requirements, and the service invalidates approvals and queued work when relevant versions change.

tour.title: Run Durable Background Jobs
tour.description: Scheduled content and other deferred workflows move through a PostgreSQL transactional job outbox. The queue uses deduplicated enqueueing, skip-locked claims and leases, while the worker supplies heartbeat, retry and graceful shutdown behavior. The scheduler coordinates periodic enqueueing with an advisory lock, connecting the API transactions introduced earlier to reliable work outside a request.

tour.title: Track External Operation Outcomes
tour.description: When a job is ready to send or publish, operation services revalidate authorization and account conditions before crossing the provider boundary. They commit ledger checkpoints before transaction-free provider calls, then distinguish confirmed effects, safe retries, failures and ambiguous results that require reconciliation. The provider protocol and stateful simulator make this behavior locally demonstrable, including failures and quotas, without establishing completed real Meta integration.

tour.title: Explain Reports with Evidence
tour.description: Reports turn persisted workflow state into canonical workspace-filtered SQL metrics and navigable evidence. Today can use live rows, while historical reports use immutable generations with saved membership and measurements so links keep explaining the same numbers after source state changes. Regeneration appends a revision rather than replacing that historical explanation, connecting reporting back to the durable records created by earlier workflows.

tour.title: Preserve Audit and Retention
tour.description: The historical evidence introduced in the previous step must remain honest as sensitive source content ages out. Retention runs idempotent batches that redact or delete eligible data while preserving audit rows and report evidence; failed-event deletion records source gaps atomically so regeneration cannot silently undercount. Append-only audit writing stays in the caller transaction, and lifecycle tests exercise snapshot stability, retention and tenant boundaries together.

tour.title: Reproduce the Local Environment
tour.description: With the workflows understood, use the development guide to assemble the same API, worker, workspace and simulated demonstration locally. Compose supplies a health-checked PostgreSQL instance with persistent storage, while Alembic connects application model metadata to ordered schema changes. This setup makes the transaction and evidence boundaries from earlier steps inspectable in a real local database.

tour.title: Assess Verification and Readiness
tour.description: Finish by checking how CI, deterministic AI evaluations and browser scenarios exercise the boundaries you have followed. Scenario E verifies report agreement and generation-bound evidence, and the later QA record supersedes the original local AC-E3 reporting gap. The same QA record keeps wider Gate 1 acceptance open, so passing local regressions must be read alongside the remaining review and acceptance work.
